note: The repository currently has no Controller runtime input contract or Controller implementation. This sample demonstrates the proposal's decision-package output shape only; scores and values are invented.

sample_report.summary: P-110 failed on aircraft N123AB at MIA. P-120 is authorized and traceable at DFW, with an estimated transfer arrival at 13:00Z. Operations identifies flight FX103 and package redistribution as the main service impacts.
key_findings: Maintenance history contains three recent P-110 failures; the current work order estimates three hours of repair after the part is ready.
P-120 is not in MIA stock but is available at DFW and has current mock authorization and traceability evidence.
FX103 carries 1,200 packages, including 700 priority packages; alternate capacity is limited.

risk_metrics: Some packages may miss the planned service window.
ranked_options.trade_off: Uses an authorized replacement part and avoids a full aircraft swap, but depends on the DFW transfer arriving on time.

risk_metrics: Substitute aircraft has less package capacity than the affected load.
Another flight may be disrupted by moving the aircraft.
ranked_options.trade_off: May restore flight service without waiting for the part, but costs more and leaves more packages without a confirmed route.

recommended_recovery_path.rationale: The replacement part has current mock authorization and traceability evidence, and repair is estimated to complete within the case need-by time. The transfer and package impacts remain uncertain.
assumptions: The DFW transfer estimate remains valid.
Current schedule and package-load data are accurate.
risks: Transfer delay could push repair completion later.
The score is illustrative and has not been produced by a runtime Controller.

sample_report.next_action: Maintenance/airworthiness authority reviews the repair and part evidence; Operations lead reviews the flight and package impacts. No operational action is taken until humans approve.
